title: Little Red Riding Hood and the wolf.
lines: Once upon a time there was a little girl.
She always wore a red hood on her head.
She had been given that hood by her grandma.
That's why everyone called her Little Red Riding Hood.
One morning Mummy said: Little Red Riding Hood, Grandma is ill.
Will you take her a basket?
There's cake in it, and a bottle of juice, and a few apples.
Yes, Mummy!
said Little Red Riding Hood.
Mummy gave her a kiss.
Be careful, she said.
Stay on the path in the forest, and don't talk to strangers.
I promise, Mummy!
Little Red Riding Hood took the basket and set off.
Grandma's little house was on the other side of the forest.
It was a lovely day.
The sun shone through the trees.
The birds were singing.
Tweet, tweet!
Little Red Riding Hood skipped along the path.
But behind a thick tree someone was watching.
It was the big grey wolf.
He was hungry.
Very, very hungry.
Good morning, little girl, said the wolf in a sweet voice.
Where are you going?
Little Red Riding Hood had forgotten.
She wasn't supposed to talk to strangers.
To my grandma, she said.
She lives in the little house by the three big oak trees.
She's ill.
How sweet, said the wolf.
Look, there are some beautiful flowers over there.
Pick a few for your grandma.
That will make her happy.
Little Red Riding Hood thought that was a good idea.
She left the path and picked flowers.
A yellow one, a blue one, a purple one.
Meanwhile the wolf ran as fast as he could to Grandma's house.
Knock, knock, knock.
Who's there?
asked Grandma.
It's me, Little Red Riding Hood, said the wolf in a high voice.
Come in, dear.
The wolf went inside.
Grandma got a terrible fright and quickly hid in the big wardrobe.
The wolf put on Grandma's nightcap.
He climbed into bed and pulled the covers up to his nose.
A little later Little Red Riding Hood arrived.
The door was open.
Grandma?
she called.
She walked to the bed.
But Grandma looked very strange.
Grandma, what big ears you have!
All the better to hear you with, said the wolf.
Grandma, what big eyes you have!
All the better to see you with.
Grandma, what big hands you have!
All the better to hold you with.
Grandma, what a big mouth you have!
All the better to eat you with!
And the wolf jumped out of bed.
Little Red Riding Hood screamed as loud as she could.
Help!
Help!
Outside a hunter was walking by.
He heard the screaming and ran inside.
What's going on here?
he shouted in a deep voice.
The wolf got the fright of his life.
He dropped the nightcap and jumped out of the window.
He ran into the forest, as far as he could, and he never came back.
The wardrobe door opened.
There was Grandma!
She was a bit dusty, but she was perfectly fine.
Grandma!
cried Little Red Riding Hood, and she flew into her arms.
The hunter helped Grandma back into her bed.
Little Red Riding Hood gave her the flowers and the basket.
They ate cake together and drank juice.
The hunter got a piece too.
Mmm, yummy!
Grandma already felt much better.
When Little Red Riding Hood went home, she thought about it.
From now on I'll always stay on the path, she said.
And I'll never talk to strangers again.
Not even if they're very nice.
Mummy was very happy that her girl came home safely.
And the wolf?
He never dared to come near again.
The end.
